purpose: Unchanged established requested-fact scope,projected without reader answers or grades for a fresh grader.

grading_standard.correct: Every requested fact correct and supported,without contradiction/unresolved requested ruling.
grading_standard.partial: Missing/unresolved requested fact without material contradiction.

questions.question: An Exile takes the Oathkeeper title during their Act phase. When can they first win as Usurper, and what happens if someone takes the title away meanwhile?
questions.expected_answer: At their next Wake they check victory before flipping Oathkeeper to Usurper, so cannot yet win as Usurper; if still Usurper at the following Wake they win. Losing the title prevents this; a new holder receives it Oathkeeper-side. At end of round eight an existing Usurper can win under the ordered endgame rules.
requested_expected_facts: Victory is checked before the next-Wake Oathkeeper-to-Usurper flip; ordinary Usurper victory is at the following Wake if retained.
Losing the title prevents that win; transfer/retaking uses the Oathkeeper side and restarts the sequence.
An existing Usurper can instead win at the end-of-round-eight priority check, potentially before the following Wake.

questions.question: List all four Oaths, their matching Visions, and the extra universal requirement for a Visionary win. Do ties for most count for a Vision?
questions.expected_answer: Supremacy/Conquest: most sites; People/Rebellion: People’s Favor; Protection/Sanctuary: most relics and banners combined; Devotion/Faith: Darkest Secret. Exile must have the Vision revealed, fulfill it at Wake (or the round-eight check), and at least three Visions must have been drawn from the world deck. Most means strictly more than every other player, not a tie.
requested_expected_facts: Four mappings: Supremacy–Conquest, People–Rebellion, Protection–Sanctuary, Devotion–Faith.
Visionary win requires an Exile with a revealed true Vision and fulfilled goal.
At least three Visions must have been drawn from the world deck.
Most for a Vision means strictly more than each other player; ties do not count.

questions.question: When are end dice rolled, what results end the game, and can an Exile Oathkeeper permit such a roll?
questions.expected_answer: Only at end of rounds five/six/seven with Chancellor or Citizen Oathkeeper: 6 / 5–6 / 3–6 respectively. Exile Oathkeeper prevents the roll. Eighth round ends automatically.
requested_expected_facts: Roll only at the ends of rounds five, six, and seven when Chancellor or a Citizen is Oathkeeper.
End results are respectively 6; 5–6; 3–6.
An Exile Oathkeeper/Usurper prevents the roll.

questions.question: At round eight, what is the complete victory priority including simultaneous Visions and Citizens?
questions.expected_answer: Empire if Chancellor/Citizen Oathkeeper, then Exile Usurper, then qualifying Exile Visionary (Conquest > Rebellion > Sanctuary > Faith), then Empire fallback. Each Empire win is Chancellor unless a Citizen fulfills the Successor goal, who wins alone instead.
requested_expected_facts: At automatic round-eight ending: Imperial Oathkeeper → Empire; otherwise Exile Usurper; otherwise qualifying revealed Exile Vision; otherwise Empire fallback.
Simultaneous Vision priority is Conquest, Rebellion, Sanctuary, Faith.
Every Empire win is Chancellor unless a Citizen meeting the Successor goal replaces them and wins alone.

questions.question: Give the Successor goal for each Oath. May a Citizen win by a revealed Vision or becoming Usurper?
questions.expected_answer: Supremacy: more relics+banners than Chancellor and every other Citizen; People: Darkest Secret; Protection: People’s Favor; Devotion: Grand Scepter. Citizens do not win by Usurper or Vision, only replace a Chancellor win via succession.
requested_expected_facts: Supremacy Successor has more combined relics and banners than Chancellor and every other Citizen.
People Successor holds Darkest Secret; Protection holds People’s Favor; Devotion holds Grand Scepter.
Citizens cannot win by a revealed true Vision or Usurper.

questions.question: Resolve the People’s Favor at Wake, including the Mob side, its last favor, and when the Mob threshold is checked.
questions.expected_answer: First choose to put one board favor on it or move one from it to least-full bank (choose ties); it cannot lose its last favor, so at one must add if able, otherwise nothing. Repeat that step once if already Mob. After these steps flip to Mob if six or more favor. Then check Exile wins, flip Oathkeeper, and resolve optional opportunity-site income.
requested_expected_facts: At Wake choose adding one own-board favor or moving one banner favor to a least-full bank, choosing ties.
Cannot remove last favor: with one, add if able, otherwise do nothing.
If already Mob, repeat the choice once.
Check six-or-more threshold after those steps; newly turning Mob does not retroactively repeat the step.

questions.question: What happens in Rest, in order, and how do Citizen Supply and saved Supply work?
questions.expected_answer: Return favor from denizens/edifices to matching banks; secrets from denizens/edifices/relics to acting board and flip own facedown secrets up; Exile/Chancellor refresh to personal-bank-warband space, Citizen to exact Chancellor marker space including leftmost; add remaining unspent Supply by moving left, capped at leftmost; optional Rest powers once each any order.
requested_expected_facts: Return denizen/edifice favor to matching banks.
Return denizen/edifice/relic secrets to acting board, then turn own facedown board secrets faceup.
Refresh Exile/Chancellor by personal-bank warbands and Citizen to exact Chancellor marker space, including leftmost.
Then add unspent Supply by moving extra spaces left, capped at leftmost.
Then optional Rest powers once each in any order.

questions.question: Explain Search sources/costs and how drawing a Vision differs between world deck and discard pile.
questions.expected_answer: Choose only world deck or own-region discard, 2 Supply for discard, world cost 2 at zero Visions, 3 at one/two, 4 at three–five, modified by powers (Darkest Secret makes world draw 2). Draw up to three available; from world one at a time, announce a Vision, stop immediately and increment track; discard Vision does neither. Discard all but one before playing or discarding that one.
requested_expected_facts: Choose world deck or pawn-region discard, not both.
Discard costs two; world costs two at zero Visions, three at one/two, four at three–five, subject to modifiers including Darkest Secret’s fixed two.
Draw three unless source exhaustion, a world Vision, or an applicable modifier stops/reduces it; world Vision is announced, stops draw immediately, and advances track.
Discard Vision neither stops draw nor advances track.

questions.question: Where do discarded cards and resources on them go, including a card at a remote site?
questions.expected_answer: Facedown atop next-region pile: Cradle→Provinces→Hinterland→Cradle, acting player chooses order. Base on pawn region for drawn/adviser cards; if discarding a card in a different region, use that card’s region. Favor immediately goes to matching bank; secrets to acting board facedown.
requested_expected_facts: Cards go facedown atop next-region pile, cycling Cradle→Provinces→Hinterland→Cradle.
Hand/adviser cards use pawn region; remote-site cards use their own region.
Favor immediately goes to matching suit bank; secrets go to acting board facedown.

questions.question: How do adviser limits, facedown restrictions, revealing later, and replacing a true Vision work?
questions.expected_answer: Three advisers including facedown; facedown has no suit/banner/power, any card can be held thus. Before playing over limit discard an adviser, respecting locks and any new changed limit. Minor action may play facedown adviser faceup as searched (site/advisers/revealed Vision as legal) or discard it. True faceup Vision only Exile revealed slot, not adviser, replaces/discards existing Vision. Cannot simply discard faceup adviser at will.
requested_expected_facts: Three total advisers, counting facedown; discard before playing over the limit.
Respect locked advisers and use a new lower adviser limit before playing a limit-changing card (lowest applicable limit).
Facedown advisers lack suit/restriction banner/power; any card can be held facedown.
Later minor action plays facedown adviser faceup under Search play destinations/restrictions, or discards it.
A faceup true Vision is Exile-only in separate revealed slot, not an adviser, and replaces/discards old revealed Vision.
Faceup advisers cannot simply be discarded at will.

questions.question: What are Muster and both Trade costs, eligible cards, gains, destinations, and limitations when no advisers match?
questions.expected_answer: Only empty denizen/intact edifice at pawn site, no favor/secrets; not relic/ruin. Muster 1 Supply+one favor on card → two personal-bank warbands to board, purple for Citizen. Trade 1 Supply; one secret on card → one favor+one per matching faceup adviser from matching bank; or two favor on card → one shared-bank secret per matching faceup adviser (zero if none). Finite source shortfall gives as much as possible.
requested_expected_facts: Eligible empty denizen/intact edifice at pawn site, with no favor/secrets; relics/ruins ineligible and remote rule insufficient.
Muster: one Supply and one favor on card, gain two personal-bank warbands on board; Citizens gain purple.

Both Trade options cost one Supply: one secret on card gains one plus matching-faceup-adviser count in favor from matching bank; two favor on card gains matching-faceup-adviser count in shared-bank secrets.
Facedown advisers do not match; zero matching advisers yields zero secrets in second option (and base one favor in first).
Finite sources limit gains to available pieces; secrets unlimited.

questions.question: How do you Recover a relic versus either banner, and what happens to the old banner resources?
questions.expected_answer: 1 Supply; facedown relic at pawn site only at printed site cost, then take faceup personal bank. Either banner from anywhere, even yourself: pay more favor/secrets than old amount, stack new payment. People’s Favor flips off Mob and old favor distributes singly along banks away from deck from any starting suit wrapping. Darkest Secret: take one old secret, previous holder gets rest (self gets all; bank remainder stays bank).
requested_expected_facts: Recover costs one Supply.
Recover only facedown relic at pawn site at printed site cost; take faceup into personal bank.
Either banner from anywhere/self/shared bank: pay strictly more of appropriate resource than existing amount and replace old stack with payment.
People’s Favor returns off Mob; old favor distributes singly to banks starting with any suit, moving away from world deck, wrapping.
Darkest Secret new holder takes one old secret, previous holder gets rest; self gets all, bank remainder stays bank.

questions.question: When is another player’s Darkest Secret safe or recoverable? Include no advisers, no cards, and a ruin-only site.
questions.expected_answer: Recoverable if at least one suited card at holder’s pawn site matches none of their faceup advisers; no faceup advisers does not protect it if suited card exists. Empty/ruin-only site protects it; ignore suits absent on ruins/facedown advisers. Can recover from self or shared bank freely, still paying cost.
requested_expected_facts: Another player’s banner is recoverable if at least one suited card at their pawn site matches none of their faceup advisers.
No faceup advisers does not protect when a suited site card exists.
Empty and ruin-only sites protect; ruins and facedown advisers have no suit.

questions.question: Explain legal Campaign defender and target selection, including remote sites and a same-site relic target.
questions.expected_answer: 2 Supply; defender another player ruling pawn site or whose pawn there, or bandits if no player rules it. At least one target at pawn site; if defender rules it must target it. May target any defender sites anywhere; relics/banners or pawn+favor only if their pawn is at attacker site. Relic target of co-located defender satisfies local target requirement. Pawn+favor adds two defense dice; sites one each; relic printed shields; banners resource count.
requested_expected_facts: Defender is another player ruling attacker site or with pawn there; bandits may be chosen if no player rules site.
At least one local target; must target attacker site when defender rules it.
May additionally target defender’s sites anywhere.
Relics/banners/pawn-and-favor may be targeted only if defender pawn is at attacker site.
Co-located defender relic satisfies local-target requirement.

questions.question: How are Campaign attack/defense calculated, and how do skulls, hollow swords, ties and sacrifices work?
questions.expected_answer: Attacker chooses up to board-force warbands worth of attack dice. Defense shields multiplied by each double (x2,x4,...), plus warbands at targeted sites and defender board if pawn at attacker or targeted site; bandits one per targeted site. Attack skulls kill own force immediately; paired hollow swords count one, lone hollow zero. Attack must strictly exceed defense; may sacrifice force warbands +1 each, exactly enough to win, no excess; if unable/decline defender wins.
requested_expected_facts: Attacker chooses dice up to warbands in force.
Defense is shields multiplied exponentially by doubles plus defending site warbands and board warbands only with pawn at attacker/targeted site; bandits one per targeted bandit site.
Skulls immediately kill own force warbands; full swords count, paired hollow swords add one, lone hollow adds zero.
Attack must strictly exceed defense; ties/lower defend.
May sacrifice surviving force for plus one each, exactly enough to win, never excess; if not winning, defender wins.

questions.question: After an attacker wins, resolve defeat and all targets, including choosing zero garrisons, banner seizure, and banishment.
questions.expected_answer: Defeated force kills half rounded down; remaining returns to board; defeated effects. Attacker may move any number including zero from force onto targeted sites, takes all targeted relics/banners; seized banners burn two resources to min one, People’s Favor becomes Mob. If pawn+favor targeted may banish to legal chosen site for no Supply and may burn half favor rounded down. Shrouded Wood can override destination. Victory effects then end-discard plans.
requested_expected_facts: Defeated side kills half remaining force rounded down and returns survivors to board.
Resolve defeated battle-plan effects.
Attacker may garrison targeted sites with any number including zero and takes all targeted relics/banners.
Seized banner loses two resources to minimum one; People’s Favor flips Mob.
Pawn-and-favor target permits independent free legal banishment and burning half board favor rounded down.
Shrouded Wood can override who chooses banishment destination.
Then resolve victorious effects and end-of-Campaign plan discards.

questions.question: What changes in a Campaign involving Imperial defenders or a Citizen attacking another Imperial player?
questions.expected_answer: Citizen attacker against Chancellor/Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign; Citizen targeted by Chancellor likewise. Imperial defender gets Chancellor automatically as Ally; non-attacker Citizens may join with permission if pawn at targeted site or attacker site. Activate defender/allies modifiers, share side powers and battle plans, one use per plan paid by user, never another’s advisers; qualifying allied board warbands defend. Chancellor chooses losses; survivors at sites go Chancellor board, Citizens keep own board survivors. Declared defender decides contested timing/order. Oathkeeper defense bonus shared even non-Supremacy.
requested_expected_facts: Citizen attacking Chancellor/Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign; Citizen attacked by Chancellor likewise.
Imperial defender automatically gets Chancellor Ally; other non-attacker Citizens may join with permission and pawn at attacker/targeted site.
Activate defender/allied modifiers and applicable shared title defense bonus, including non-Supremacy.
Battle plans may be used at Imperial sites/own advisers, never others’ advisers; user pays, same plan once per Campaign/not by multiple users.
Allied board warbands defend only if pawn at attacker/targeted site.
Chancellor chooses defending losses; surviving site warbands go Chancellor board, Citizen-board survivors stay there.
Applicable powers are shared across the defending side, as clarified by errata; declared defender decides contested timing/order/shared-power user.

questions.question: State all base Travel costs and what happens when a facedown destination is revealed. How do fixed costs, increases and free Travel interact?
questions.expected_answer: Cradle→Cradle 1, Provinces 2, Hinterland 4; Provinces→any other site 2; Hinterland→Hinterland 3, Provinces 2, Cradle 4. Move pawn, reveal site and add printed favor/secrets from shared bank and facedown relics from relic deck. Apply fixed-number Travel cost first then other modifiers; spend-no-Supply overrides all increases. Pawn movement does not move site warbands.
requested_expected_facts: Base matrix: Cradle to Cradle/Provinces/Hinterland 1/2/4; Provinces to any other site 2; Hinterland to Cradle/Provinces/Hinterland 4/2/3.
Reveal facedown destination and place printed favor/secrets and facedown relics there.
Apply fixed cost first, then other increases/decreases; spend-no-Supply overrides all cost increases.

questions.question: How can Citizenship be offered and accepted during play, and what may or must be exchanged?
questions.expected_answer: Grand Scepter holder (not taken this turn) offers any Exile including self exactly one Reliquary relic plus optional binding exchange favor,secrets,banners,non-Reliquary relics. Accepted: flip Citizen, replace all board/map warbands purple as available with recipient choosing shortfall removals/replacements, discard revealed Vision, Usurper→Oathkeeper, end Act if own turn, refresh full. Exchange agreed items; Chancellor gains uncovered mandatory modifier. All Imperials rule purple sites. Reliquary relics inaccessible to Campaign/Recover, powers unusable, do not count goals.
requested_expected_facts: Grand Scepter holder, not on turn taken, offers any Exile including self.
Must promise exactly one Reliquary relic; optional binding exchanges of favor/secrets/banners/non-Reliquary relics.
Acceptance flips Citizen and replaces own board/map warbands purple, recipient choosing shortfall removals/replacements.
Discard revealed Vision, Usurper flips Oathkeeper, end Act if own turn, refresh full Supply.
Exchange promised items and Chancellor gains uncovered mandatory Reliquary modifier.

questions.question: Describe the Chronicle’s new Oath choice, Citizenship turnover, and world-deck rebuilding, including why the top stack is not 14 cards.
questions.expected_answer: Vision-only winner uses matching Oath; other/multiple-method win chooses any different Oath. Exile winner flips all Citizens even boxed to Exile then may offer other Exiles except newly flipped; accepted map garrisons replaced one each by winner warband (ignore normal offer). Rebuild remaining denizens: ten+two random Visions=12 top, fifteen+three Visions=18 middle, remaining denizens bottom. Chronicle aid 12 denizens+2 is erroneous.
requested_expected_facts: Vision-only winner chooses matching Oath; other/multiple-method victory chooses a different Oath.
Exile winner flips all Citizens including boxed to Exile, then may offer other Exiles except just-flipped, not self, ignoring normal offer rules.
Acceptors flip Citizen; replace garrisons at their ruled sites with one winner-color warband per site.
Rebuild remaining denizens: top ten denizens plus two random Visions equals twelve; middle fifteen plus remaining three equals eighteen; remaining denizens bottom.
Chronicle aid twelve-denizens-plus-two is erroneous and would incorrectly make fourteen.
